Method/Phylogenetic inference

Bayesian phylogeny

Jointly estimate a time-scaled tree, molecular clock, and population model, with uncertainty on every estimate.

When to use this method

Use when

  • You need credible intervals on dates, such as when a lineage was introduced.
  • You want phylodynamic estimates, such as population growth, reproduction numbers, or migration between locations.
  • The dataset is small enough to run in reasonable time, typically hundreds to a few thousand short genomes, or a subsample of a larger collection.

Skip this method when

  • The dataset is large or results are needed routinely and quickly. Use Time-scaled phylogeny instead.
  • Dates are missing or there is little temporal signal. Use Maximum likelihood phylogeny instead.

Operation

Phylogenetic inference

Implementations

  • BEAST X
  • BEAST 2

Needs

Recombination-filtered alignment or Full genome alignment or SNP-only alignment, Collection dates

Produces

Time-scaled tree

Trees, clock rates, and population parameters are sampled together with Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), so the results describe a range of plausible histories rather than a single tree. Summarize the posterior trees as a maximum clade credibility tree for display.

Runs can take hours to days. Check convergence before interpreting results: effective sample sizes above 200 for key parameters, with independent runs that agree.

Used by protocols

Specified by

  • Viral phylogenomic surveillanceStep 4

Other methods for this operation

  • Maximum likelihood phylogenyFind the tree that best explains the alignment under a substitution model, with branch lengths in substitutions per site.
  • Time-scaled phylogenyRescale an existing tree, usually a maximum likelihood tree, so branch lengths are in time and ancestral nodes are dated.
